approval.case_selection_rule: Sort weeks by (fold, week, group_id) ascending. C1 = first with fallback == False and gate.all_rejected == False; C2 = first with fallback == True; C3 = first with fallback == False and 0 < gate.gate_passed_candidates < gate.evaluated_candidates and key != C1 key; C4 = first with fallback == False and gate.gate_passed_candidates == gate.evaluated_candidates. Deduplicate by (fold, week, group_id). Mechanical, text-blind rule (ST9-03, amended ST9-04 after C1/C3 key collision, before deployment).

explanation.text: For bundle B01_CA_FOODS_3 in week 1, the approved action sets tau to 0.6 with an empty multiplier set, so no multiplier adjustments are applied. Of 8 candidate actions evaluated, 4 were rejected for capacity and 2 for service level, leaving 2 that passed the gate, including the approved action. The supplied record does not include the base policy's tau or multiplier values, so the exact change from base must be confirmed against the policy configuration before this is reported as a delta. The action passed because it cleared both the capacity and service-level checks that eliminated the other six candidates.

Bundle B05_TX_FOODS_3, week 1 is approved with tau=0.6 and an empty multiplier set, so no multiplier adjustments are applied. The provided record does not include the base policy parameters, so this summary cannot state the exact change from base beyond the approved tau and the absence of multipliers. The gate counts do not reconcile: 10 candidates were evaluated, and 3 (capacity) plus 7 (service-level) rejections account for all 10, which leaves no evident passing candidate. Verify the gate log and confirm which candidate was approved before acting on this action.

This week's approved action for bundle B02_CA_FOODS_1 (week 1) sets the policy parameter tau to 0.7 with an empty multiplier set, so no multiplier adjustments are applied. The input does not include the base policy's parameter values, so the size of the change from base cannot be stated; the only specified difference is tau = 0.7 and no multipliers. Of the 20 candidates evaluated, 9 were rejected for capacity and 8 for service level. If those rejection categories are mutually exclusive, 3 candidates passed both checks, and the approved action is the one that cleared the gate. The input does not confirm exclusivity, so the passing count should be verified against the candidate-level log.

For bundle B05_TX_FOODS_3 in week 1, the approved action sets the policy parameter tau to 0.6 with no multipliers applied. Relative to the base policy, the change is confined to this tau setting, and the inputs do not specify the base tau value, so the size of the shift should be confirmed against the base configuration. The action passed the gate because all 9 candidates were evaluated and none were rejected for capacity or for service level, so the selected candidate cleared both constraints. Because the action carries no multipliers, no additional scaling was applied beyond tau.

stage4.h2_input_decision: H2 primary input model: LightGBM 11-quantile (ST4-08). Chosen to keep the ST3-07 ACI contract unchanged (q0.05/q0.95 base interval, 28-day fixed feedback delay, online update rule, initial state). The 12-fold WQL ranking between A3 and LightGBM is NOT used for this selection: those folds are the preregistered final evaluation set, and selecting on them would couple model selection with H2 evaluation. Disclosure: Stage 3 already produced and reported the LightGBM ACI coverage (0.8885 after calibration), so this decision was not made blind to prior evaluation results. A3-based ACI on the q0.10/q0.90 base interval is theoretically possible but a different experimental setting; deferred to exploratory follow-up. Stage 4 does not re-optimize any interval parameters.
